subject: [Status] Hosted inference — sustained P50 latency drift affecting AxiomAI routes
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@axiomai.com>, ops@axiomai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Status] Hosted inference — sustained P50 latency drift affecting AxiomAI routes

Hi Erin / Axiom ops team,

We’re writing to let you know we’ve identified a sustained elevation in P50 request latency for requests routed to your production model variant since ~08:40 PDT this morning. The behavior is limited to hosted endpoints using the us-west-1 pool and is impacting your routing percentage of traffic (~18% of requests seeing elevated P50).

What we know so far:
- Symptom: median (P50) response times increased from ~120ms to ~560ms for typical short-generation requests.
- Scope: concentrated on AxiomAI's primary model route (route_id: axiom-prod-v2) in us-west-1.
- Impact: higher request latency (P50) and occasional increased tail for medium-length prompts. No generation truncation or data loss observed.

Immediate actions in progress:
- We’ve opened an incident (INC-20250614-axiomai) and our on-call is triaging kernel selection and batching configuration for the affected pool.
- Temporary mitigations: routing is set to prefer an alternate compatible pool in us-east-1 for new sessions while we investigate. This will be automatic and should reduce latency for new requests within the next 10–15 minutes.

We’ll update you with findings and a timeline for resolution; next status at 10:00 PDT or sooner if anything changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your SLAs and are treating it with high priority.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:28:15 -0700
Subject: Re: [Status] Hosted inference — sustained P50 latency drift affecting AxiomAI routes

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the quick heads-up. A couple quick questions from our side:

1) Does the fallback to us-east-1 change session affinity or break existing long-lived sessions? We have conversational sessions that rely on KV cache locality.
2) Will there be any token-count or cost implications from the reroute?

We’ve already seen a spike in user-reported slow replies for a subset of sessions; if there’s an ETA for remediation that helps us decide whether to redirect traffic on our side as well.

— Erin
Erin Walsh
Head of SRE, AxiomAI

Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:45:03 -0700
Subject: RE: [Status] Hosted inference — sustained P50 latency drift affecting AxiomAI routes

Sofia / Marissa — quick notes from triage: 
- Initial metric correlation points to an atypical kernel selection path being preferred after a recent scheduling tweak in the us-west-1 serving pool (INFRA-2731). This increases per-request prep time for short sequences.
- No evidence of hardware degradation. Memory/KV eviction rates normal.

Immediate plan:
1) Force consistent kernel set for axiom-prod-v2 in us-west-1 (rollback scheduling tweak); will roll this to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 minutes.
2) Keep the us-east-1 fallback in place for new sessions until P50 returns to baseline.
3) Capture and share P50/P95 graphs and playbook snippets (see attached PDF).

Sofia — if you can confirm the fallback routing didn’t invalidate a significant number of active sessions for them, call that out to Erin.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@axiomai.com>, ops@axiomai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 10:02:10 -0700
Subject: RE: [Status] Hosted inference — sustained P50 latency drift affecting AxiomAI routes

Erin — quick clarification on session behavior: the automatic fallback is applied only to new session initiations and to requests where the existing KV cache cannot be used safely across regions. Existing long-lived sessions pinned to us-west-1 will remain there and continue to use their local KV cache. The majority of impacted requests we observed are short, stateless calls (queries, small completions).

Cost note: there is no intentional token-count increase from the reroute; outbound egress between regions is metered per cloud provider but for the traffic volumes we saw we do not expect a material billing change for AxiomAI. If you’d like, your account team can provide a short delta estimate after the incident.

We are proceeding with Ben’s rollback plan now. Next update in ~20–30 minutes or sooner if the rollback finishes early.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we know this is disruptive.

— Sofia
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 10:29:45 -0700
Subject: [RESOLVED] Hosted inference — P50 latency restored for AxiomAI routes (INC-20250614-axiomai)

Status: Resolved for user-visible latency (P50) — rollback of the scheduling tweak in us-west-1 completed and verified.

Summary:
- Time detected: 2025-06-14 08:40 PDT
- Mitigation: forced kernel selection parity + temporary routing of new sessions to us-east-1
- Time resolved: 2025-06-14 10:24 PDT
- Impact: elevated P50 for ~18% of AxiomAI requests. P95 remained within SLA bounds; no request truncation or data loss.

Follow-ups we’re working on:
- Postmortem write-up and timeline (link below) with root cause and long-term remediation.
- A change to the scheduling rollout process to include targeted canary checks for kernel selection variance (JIRA INFRA-2731).

Attachments: a short P50 trend graph attached (axiomai_p50_graphs.png) and our playbook for rollback (mitigation_playbook.pdf).

If you’d like a quick 15-min post-incident call to walk through the timeline and next steps with engineering, please propose a time and we’ll coordinate.

— Sofia
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear updates and for resolving quickly. We’d appreciate a short postmortem that includes:
- Confirmation that no KV cache corruption or session loss occurred for long-lived sessions.
- A short explanation of the scheduling tweak and why it surfaced for this route.
- Expected rollout plan and guardrails for INFRA-2731.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync Monday 2025-06-16 at 09:30 PDT (if that works for your team)? If not, propose alternatives.

— Erin
